critique.good: The course bands establish a clear hierarchy, and the rows have a consistent rhythm. Dish names are easy to find, prices align in a compact column, and descriptions and allergens remain within three lines.
critique.problems: Several dish names wrap, and the dessert allergen list is somewhat cramped. The descriptions use the available height well, although their short lines make the menu feel dense.
critique.cause: The 150px dish column leaves some names on two lines; the 134px allergen column forces the longest list onto three lines. The 220px description column keeps all descriptions to three lines in this render.

critique.good: The wider description column makes the ingredients easier to read and brings the risotto description down to two lines. Headers and prices remain intact.
critique.problems: Several dish names fragment into three lines, weakening the first scanning column. The dessert allergen list stretches to five lines and makes that row substantially taller; its parenthetical qualifiers are separated from their allergens.
critique.cause: The 115px dish column and 104px allergen column are too narrow for their longer entries. The 285px description column takes space that would help both.

critique.good: More dish names fit on one line, and the wider allergen column keeps most lists relatively easy to scan. The course groups and prices remain clear.
critique.problems: Descriptions become narrow stacks of up to five lines, making the table much taller and leaving large empty areas in other cells. The extra width does not keep every dish name on one line.
critique.cause: The 170px description column is too narrow for the longest prose, while the 170px dish and 164px allergen columns consume space that could shorten those descriptions.

critique.good: The course bands and consistent three-line dish rows create a clear rhythm. Dish names, prices and headers are easy to scan, and descriptions wrap without splitting words.
critique.problems: The dessert allergen list splits “Tree nuts” across lines, making that allergen slower to read. Every dish name also wraps, though the first column is relatively generous.
critique.cause: At 129px, Allergens has 108px of text space, which is too narrow to keep “Tree nuts” together in its current line flow. The 145px Dish column still cannot fit the full names on one line.

critique.good: The balanced rows and clear course hierarchy are retained. The wider allergen column keeps “Tree nuts” together, and all descriptions remain within three lines.
critique.problems: The dessert allergen qualifier “(hazelnut)” sits alone on the last line, separated from “Tree nuts”. The description column is slightly compressed while the extra allergen width does not reduce row height.
critique.cause: The 144px Allergens column changes the line breaks but does not have enough room to keep “Tree nuts (hazelnut)” together after the preceding items. Description is reduced to 220px.

critique.good: The wider Description column gives its text a more relaxed measure, and prices and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The dessert allergen list takes four lines, splitting “Tree nuts” and leaving “(hazelnut)” alone. This makes the final row taller and less cohesive without reducing the height of the description-led rows.
critique.cause: Allergens is only 124px wide, leaving 103px for text. The additional width assigned to the 250px Description column does not remove a line from any row.

critique.good: The course bands and consistent three-line descriptions give the menu a steady rhythm. Prices are easy to scan, headers stay intact, and allergen lists remain readable.
critique.problems: Every dish name wraps, weakening the first scan down the menu. The dessert allergen list breaks “Tree nuts” across lines.
critique.cause: The 135px dish column is too narrow for the full names, while the 139px allergen column leaves too little room for that phrase in its current line.

critique.good: All descriptions and allergen lists fit within three lines, and the wider allergen column keeps “Tree nuts” together. Course groups and prices remain easy to scan.
critique.problems: Every dish name wraps, and the dessert allergen list leaves “(hazelnut)” isolated on its last line. The extra allergen width does little for most rows.
critique.cause: The 130px dish column constrains names, while the 159px allergen column is still not wide enough to keep “Tree nuts (hazelnut)” together in the dessert row.

critique.good: Several dish names fit on one line, making the first column easier to scan. Headers, prices, and individual words remain intact.
critique.problems: Three descriptions grow to four lines, producing noticeably taller rows and uneven rhythm. Two main-course names still wrap, and the dessert allergen list splits “Tree nuts.”
critique.cause: The 165px dish column takes space from the 210px description and 129px allergen columns, without being wide enough to keep every dish name on one line.

understanding.purpose: Help diners choose dishes by course, ingredients, price and allergens.
understanding.reading: Diners scan the course groups and dish names first, then read descriptions and check prices and allergens for individual choices. Each row should remain easy to follow across the table.
groups: Dish and Description belong together: the name identifies the choice and the description explains it.
Price and Allergens are compact decision aids that diners may compare across dishes.
keep_intact: Individual words in dish names, descriptions and allergen lists
Price values and their currency symbols
may_wrap: Allergen lists between items; their wrapping can often fit within height already created by a description

bad.why: The dish column has only 74px of text space, less than its longest unbreakable word. That forces a word split in a row identifier, while the allergen column receives more space than it needs.

contrast.why: The dish column has only 74px of text space, less than its longest unbreakable word. That forces a word split in a row identifier, while the allergen column receives more space than it needs.

final.rationale: r2A gives the descriptions the most room while keeping dish names readable in two lines and the longest allergen list in three. The five dish rows have a consistent height, and the short price column leaves space for the text readers need to compare. The category bands remain easy to scan across the full table.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading task rather than making columns equal.
Preserve whole words and readable row identifiers; assess wrapping across the whole row, not just the longest cell.
Give short numeric values enough space for their header, then prioritize columns carrying longer text.
specific: A 58px price column accommodates both the Price header and the prices.
In r2A, the longest description and allergen cells fit within three lines, producing consistent dish-row heights.

final.tradeoffs: r2C keeps more dish names on one line, but its narrower description column creates four-line cells and taller rows. r1C gives descriptions more room, but the dessert allergen list takes four lines.
final.uncertain: A designer might prefer r1B for its slightly wider dish and allergen columns, or r3B for its wider descriptions. The ranges are approximate, judged from the supplied renders; their endpoints have not been independently rendered. Adjustments must preserve the 562px total, with the other columns redistributed proportionally.

A.why: The narrow dish column breaks “Croquettes” across lines and forces several dish names into three lines, while the allergen column has substantial unused space.

B.why: Dish names stay intact in two lines, descriptions read comfortably, and the compact price column leaves useful space for allergens.

C.why: The generous description column reads well and dish names stay intact, but the narrow allergen column spreads the dessert allergens over four lines.

D.why: The price column is much wider than its contents need, leaving descriptions in narrow, heavily wrapped blocks and making rows tall.

E.why: Descriptions and allergens have usable space, but the narrow dish column puts two dish names on three lines and weakens scanning of the row labels.

F.why: Dish names fit in two lines, descriptions have comfortable line lengths, and prices and allergens are easy to scan without wasting much space.

reviews.unsure: B and F are very close; their small width differences produce slightly different line breaks, and either is a sound choice.

A.why: Dish names stay intact and descriptions read comfortably in three lines. The narrow price column and generous allergen column make good use of the width.

B.why: The dish column breaks “Croquettes” across lines and forces several names into three lines, while the allergen column has substantial unused space.

C.why: The equal-width columns give prices excessive space and squeeze descriptions into five or six lines, making rows tall and harder to scan.

D.why: The wide description column reads comfortably and dish names remain intact, but the dessert allergens wrap to four lines, separating “Tree nuts” across lines.

E.why: Dish names stay within two lines, descriptions have a consistent three-line rhythm, and allergens remain readable without taking space away from the prices.

F.why: Descriptions and allergens fit well, but the narrower dish column pushes two dish names onto three lines, weakening their role as row identifiers.

reviews.unsure: A is a close alternative; the preference for E rests on its slightly more balanced allocation to descriptions and allergens.
